mainTopic: How late-arriving mourners count the seven days, the final הלכה on רבי שמעון's mourning rule (with a related ruling on טריפות), and rules that set parents apart from other relatives.
overview: The גמרא asks what happens when the head of the household goes to the cemetery and another relative arrives at the house of mourning while he is away. It answers with a three-day rule: if he came back within three days, the newcomer counts with the family, and if not, the newcomer counts on his own. רב gave the same instruction to the family of הצלבוני. רבא adds that mourners who do not follow the coffin to burial start counting when they turn back at the city gate. רבי שמעון holds that a mourner who arrives from nearby even on the seventh day finishes with the family, and רבי limits this to a case where comforters are still in the house. Whether comforters who started to get up still count stays a תיקו. A report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות and like רבי שמעון in mourning is checked at its source. The טריפות half turns out to be backwards, and the mourning half is a dispute. The גמרא concludes that the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות, but is like רבי שמעון in mourning, because we follow the lenient view in אבל. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that hurrying a burial is praised for most relatives but improper for a parent, except on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, and it begins a rule about cutting back on business that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the head of the household went to the cemetery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a late-arriving mourner counts his days of mourning if the גדול הבית went with the body to the cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the head of the household went to the cemetery, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about a special case: the main family member is away at the cemetery when another relative arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a relative who arrives at the house within three days joins the family's count. Here the head of the household is not home, so it is unclear whether the newcomer still joins the family's count.

keyTerms.meaning: The head or main member of the household

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ גְּדוֹל הַבַּיִת לְבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If the head of the household went to the cemetery, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The case the גמרא assumes: another mourner arrives at the house while the head is away. Does the newcomer still join the family's count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier rule about a relative who arrives within three days and counts with the family.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a late-arriving mourner still count with the household when the גדול הבית is away at the cemetery?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: He still counts with them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that even if the head of the household went to the cemetery, the arriving mourner counts with the family.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even if the head of the household went to the cemetery, the arriving mourner counts with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי יוחנן. The head's being away does not stop the newcomer from joining the family's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אפילו ("even") shows that רבי יוחנן knew this case might seem different. He still holds that the newcomer joins the rest of the household who stayed home.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא brings a source to answer the question
He counts with them, finishing his mourning together with the family

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָלַךְ גְּדוֹל הַבַּיִת לְבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת —
phrases.english: Even if the head of the household went to the cemetery,
he counts with them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the family members who stayed home.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The arriving mourner counts with the household even if the גדול הבית is at the cemetery.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא says he counts on his own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא that says the arriving mourner counts by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really count with them? But it was taught in a ברייתא that he counts on his own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the newcomer joins the family's count. The ברייתא, about this same case, says he counts his own full seven days. Both cannot be true unless they are talking about different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
He counts on his own, keeping his own full seven days

phrases.english: He counts with them?
But it was taught: he counts on his own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the newcomer counts with the household.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that in this case he counts on his own, which directly contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: It depends on whether he came back within three days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two rulings are about different cases: whether the head of the household returned within three days or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This ruling is where he came within three days, and that ruling is where he did not come within three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by splitting the case in two, based on a three-day limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the head of the household came home within three days, the newcomer counts with the family, as רבי יוחנן said. If he did not come back within three days, the newcomer counts on his own, as the ברייתא said. Both sources stay true, each for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult (introduces an answer that reconciles two sources)
This one... and that one (each source is about a different case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The question is about the newcomer's count, but the three-day test here, as the case is explained, is about when the head of the household came back home.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he came within three days,
phrases.notes: "He" here is the head of the household returning home.

phrases.english: and that is where he did not come within three days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Within three days the newcomer counts with the family. After three days he counts on his own.

steps.title: Support from רב's instruction to the family of הצלבוני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the three-day distinction with a ruling רב gave to a mourning family.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב told the sons of הצלבוני: Those who come within three days should count with you. Those who do not come within three days should count on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the three-day line is not new. רב already used it in a real ruling for a mourning family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's instruction uses the same split: within three days you join the family's count, and after three days you count separately. This backs up the answer given in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this case: brings a similar example as support
They should count on their own

steps.whatToRemember: Three days is the dividing line. Within three days the mourners count together with the family. After three days the newcomer keeps his own count.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ רַב לִבְנֵי הַצַּלְבּוֹנִי:
phrases.english: Like that which Rav said to the sons of Hatzleponi:
Those who come within three days
should count with you,
those who do not come within three days
should count on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the three-day distinction of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The three-day dividing line between counting with the family and counting alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling for the sons of הצלבוני.

steps.title: רבא: Start counting when you turn back at the city gate
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells the people of מחוזא that mourners who do not go along to the burial start counting from when they turn back at the city gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to the people of מחוזא: You who do not follow the coffin, start counting from when you turn your faces back from the city gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related ruling: when mourning begins for those who do not go all the way to the burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מחוזא the dead were often carried far away to be buried, so most mourners did not go along. רבא rules that they do not wait for the actual burial. Their seven days begin when they part from the coffin at the city gate and turn home.

keyTerms.meaning: You turn your faces back (head home)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets when the mourning count starts for people who never reach the burial: from the moment they leave the coffin, not from the burial itself.

phrases.english: Rava said to the people of Meḥoza:
You who do not go after the coffin,
from when you turn your faces back from the city gate,
begin counting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related ruling about when mourners start their count, separate from the late-arrival question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mourners who do not accompany the coffin to burial begin counting from when they turn back at the city gate.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: Even on the seventh day he counts with them
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a mourner who arrives from a nearby place even on the seventh day joins the family's count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if he came on the seventh day from a nearby place, he counts with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's opinion from the ברייתא about a mourner who arrives late from a nearby place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling let a mourner from a nearby place join the family's count only in a limited window. רבי שמעון stretches this all the way to the seventh day: he ends his mourning together with the family instead of starting a full seven days on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: He counts with them: he finishes when the family finishes
The seventh day, the last day of שבעה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if he came on the seventh day
from a nearby place
he counts with them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the rest of the family, who started mourning earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא quoted earlier and brings up רבי שמעון's wider opinion in it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner who arrives from a nearby place, even on the seventh day, counts with the family.

steps.title: Condition: Only if comforters are still there
steps.stepSummary: רבי limits רבי שמעון's rule to a case where the arriving mourner still finds comforters in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רבי: And that is only when he came and found comforters still with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds a condition to רבי שמעון's rule from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arriving on the seventh day is not enough by itself. The mourning in the house must still be going on, which is shown by comforters still being there when he arrives. If they have already left, he cannot join the family's count.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when: a phrase that adds a condition to a rule
Comforters, people who come to comfort the mourners

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: And that is when he came and found
comforters by him.
phrases.notes: "By him" means in the mourners' house, with the family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי שמעון's rule from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seventh-day mourner counts with the family only if comforters are still present when he arrives.

steps.title: Comforters who started to get up but did not leave
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן asks about comforters who were about to leave but had not yet left. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן asked: If the comforters had stirred to get up but had not yet gotten up, what is the law? The question stands unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן tests the edge of רבי's condition, and the גמרא admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 requires comforters to be present. רב ענן asks about an in-between case: they are still sitting, but they have already started to get up to leave. Does that count as "comforters are there" or as "they already left"? The גמרא cannot decide, so it ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question about a case
Let it stand: the question is left unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is "no." It means the גמרא never settled the question either way.

phrases.english: Rav Anan asks:
If they stirred to stand up but did not stand up,
what is the law? Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a borderline case under the condition set in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether comforters who began to get up but had not left still count as "present."
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None. The question is left as תיקו.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות and רבי שמעון in mourning
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of tradition, given in two versions, רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות and רבי שמעון in אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A colleague of רבי אבא בר חייא learned from רבי אבא (that colleague was רבי זירא). Some say: a colleague of רבי זירא learned from רבי זירא (that colleague was רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא). רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a tradition that רבי יוחנן decided the הלכה in two areas, one of them being רבי שמעון's mourning rule we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree only about who heard it from whom. Both have the same rabbis, רבי זירא and רבי אבא, in swapped roles. Either way, the report says רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and like רבי שמעון. Steps 14-19 check this report, and the טריפות half turns out to be reported backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it: another version
Animals with fatal defects that make them forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This report is the starting point that the rest of the amud tests. The final ruling comes only in step 19, after the report is checked at its source.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִירִי חַבְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: A colleague of Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya learned
from Rabbi Abba,
and who was he? Rabbi Zeira,
and some say it this way:
a colleague of Rabbi Zeira learned from Rabbi Zeira,
and who was he? Rabbi Abba,
son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba,
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵיפוֹת,
phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding tereifos,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon regarding mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵיפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a הלכה ruling, said in רבי יוחנן's name, on the opinion of רבי שמעון from step 7. The report is checked in steps 14-18 and decided in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות and רבי שמעון in אבל.

steps.title: Which rulings רבי יוחנן meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the rulings: for רבי שמעון it is the seventh-day mourner rule, and for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל it is intestines whose hole is sealed by mucus, which are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Like רבי שמעון in mourning" refers to what we just said. "Like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות" refers to what we learned: intestines that were punctured but mucus seals the hole are כשר. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which specific rulings of each תנא רבי יוחנן was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא has many rulings, so the גמרא points to the exact one. For רבי שמעון it is the seventh-day mourner case from step 7. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל it is a punctured intestine plugged by mucus: since nothing leaks out, the animal is not a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a Tannaic teaching

steps.whatToRemember: A late mourner from a nearby place, even on day seven, finishes with the family if comforters are still there, and this is the הלכה like רבי שמעון. Whether comforters who started to get up still count is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: "Like Rabbi Shimon regarding mourning"
is what we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the seventh-day ruling in step 7.

phrases.english: "Like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding tereifos"
is what we learned:
Intestines that were punctured
and mucus seals them up
the animal is kosher,
these are the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which rulings step 10 is referring to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific rulings of רבי שמעון and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל רבי יוחנן meant (an unstated question).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון's seventh-day mourner rule, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling that intestines sealed by mucus are כשר.

steps.title: What is this mucus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'לֵיחָה' (mucus) is that seals the hole in the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'mucus'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'לֵיחָה' means in the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It is setting up the definition that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that intestines with a hole sealed by לֵיחָה are כשר according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Before going further, the גמרא needs to know what this substance actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: Mucus or moisture; here, the substance that seals a hole in the intestines

phrases.english: What is 'mucus'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term used in step 11

steps.title: רב כהנא defines the mucus
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that it is the fatty substance of the intestines that comes out when they are squeezed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is the fat of the intestines that comes out under pressure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question and defines לֵיחָה as fatty material from the intestines that oozes out when pressed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is clear. A hole in the intestine is sealed by this fatty substance that the intestines release when squeezed. That is the case where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said the animal is כשר.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The fat of the intestines
that comes out because of pressure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לֵיחָה is the fatty substance squeezed out of the intestines

steps.title: A scholar travels to check the rulings at their source
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed scholar wishes to learn the ruling directly from the one who said it, goes up to ארץ ישראל, and finds רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said: May I merit to go up and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master. When he went up, he found רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the next move. A scholar wants to hear the rulings from step 10 firsthand, so he travels and finds the person who reported them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rulings in step 10 came through a chain of people, and there were even two versions. Hearing it straight from the source is the best way to know which version is correct. This sets up the questions he is about to ask.

phrases.english: Someone said:
May I merit to go up
phrases.notes: Going up means traveling from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and learn the teaching
from the mouth of its master.
phrases.notes: The 'master' is the scholar who first reported this ruling, so he can hear it firsthand.

phrases.english: When he went up,
he found Rabbi Abba,
son of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story frame introducing a check of the step 10 rulings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar seeks to verify the reported rulings directly from their source

steps.title: Did you rule like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות?
steps.stepSummary: The scholar asks רבי אבא whether he really said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did the master say the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar asks רבי אבא directly whether the first ruling from step 10 is accurate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is checking the טריפות ruling first. If it is true, intestines whose hole is sealed by mucus are כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Did the master say? (a respectful way to quote someone to his face)
Defects that make an animal forbidden to eat

phrases.english: He said to him: Did the master say:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵיפוֹת?
phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in tereifos?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The scholar begins checking the reported rulings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the reported ruling following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות is accurate

steps.title: No, I said the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that he said the הלכה does NOT follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I said 'the הלכה is not.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא corrects the report. He actually ruled that the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling had been passed along backwards. Since the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a hole in the intestines sealed by mucus does not help, and the animal is a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not (like that view)

steps.confusionAlert: This reverses what step 10 reported. The original report said 'הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל'; the source himself says 'אין הלכה.' So the animal with the sealed hole is NOT כשר.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I said 'the halacha is not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and corrects the reported ruling
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling was the opposite: the הלכה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות

steps.title: What about רבי שמעון in mourning?
steps.stepSummary: The scholar asks about the second ruling: does the הלכה follow רבי שמעון in אבל?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about following רבי שמעון in mourning?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar now checks the second ruling from step 10, about רבי שמעון and mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This refers to רבי שמעון's rule from step 7: a mourner who arrives from nearby even on the seventh day joins the family's count. He wants to know if that ruling was reported correctly.

phrases.english: Following Rabbi Shimon in mourning, what about it?
phrases.notes: This is the seventh-day mourner rule from step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first reported ruling to the second
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the reported ruling following רבי שמעון in אבל is accurate

steps.title: It is a dispute among the אמוראים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that this is disputed: רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, while רב נחמן says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a dispute, as it was stated: רב חסדא said: It is the הלכה, and so said רבי יוחנן: It is the הלכה. רב נחמן said: It is not the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא does not give a single ruling. He explains that the אמוראים argue about whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי שמעון is correct, but it is not the only opinion. רב חסדא agrees with רבי יוחנן, while רב נחמן disagrees. The next step settles this dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (introduces a teaching of אמוראים)

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a dispute,
as it was stated: Rav Chisda said: It is the halacha,
phrases.notes: He means the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: and so said Rabbi Yochanan: It is the halacha.
Rav Nachman said: It is not the halacha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the mourning ruling
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The matter is disputed: רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון; רב נחמן does not

steps.title: Final ruling on both issues
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes: the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות, but it is like רבי שמעון in mourning, because שמואל said we follow the lenient view in mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות, and the הלכה is like רבי שמעון in mourning, as שמואל said: The הלכה follows the words of the one who is lenient in mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final decision on both rulings that were being checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טריפות, it follows רבי אבא's correction: the animal with a sealed hole is forbidden. For mourning, it settles the dispute using שמואל's rule that in mourning we go with the lenient opinion. רבי שמעון's view is lenient, since the late-arriving mourner joins the family's count and does not start his own full count.

keyTerms.meaning: In mourning, the הלכה follows the lenient view

steps.whatToRemember: In טריפות, the הלכה is NOT like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so a hole sealed by mucus does not make the animal כשר. In mourning, the הלכה IS like רבי שמעון, based on שמואל's rule that we follow the lenient view in אבל.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule, that the הלכה follows the lenient view in mourning, is a general principle used across many cases of אבלות.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵיפוֹת,
phrases.english: And the halacha is not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in tereifos,
and the halacha is like Rabbi Shimon in mourning.
As Shmuel said:
The halacha follows the words of the lenient one in mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵיפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides both checked rulings, settling the dispute from step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טריפות; it is like רבי שמעון in אבל, because in mourning we follow the lenient view (שמואל)

steps.title: Hurrying the burial: praised for most relatives, disgraceful for parents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that rushing out the מטה for burial is praiseworthy for most relatives. For a father or mother it is disgraceful, except on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, when it is done for the parent's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all the dead, if a person hurries out the bier, that is praiseworthy. For his father or mother, that is disgraceful. If it was ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, it is praiseworthy, because he is doing it only for the honor of his father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new practical rule about how fast to bury the dead. It sets apart parents from all other relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, burying quickly is good. With a parent, rushing looks like he wants to get the mourning over with, so it is disgraceful. On ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב the same rushing has a different reason: he does not want his parent left unburied over the holy day. So the act becomes praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Hurries out the bier, meaning he rushes the burial
The honor owed to one's father and mother

steps.confusionAlert: The same act, hurrying the burial, gets opposite ratings. What decides it is the reason behind the act: on ערב שבת it shows respect, not a wish to finish mourning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that mourning for a parent gets extra honor, and that the reason behind an act can change whether it is proper.

phrases.english: For all the dead, every one of them,
one who hurries out his bier, this is praiseworthy.
phrases.notes: Literally 'pushes his bed', meaning he rushes the bier out to be buried.

phrases.aramaic: עַל אָבִיו וְעַל אִמּוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה,
phrases.english: For his father or his mother, this is disgraceful.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת אוֹ עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: If it was Friday or the day before a Festival,
this is praiseworthy,
because he is doing it only
for the honor of his father and mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן מְדַחֶה מִטָּתוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from deciding the הלכה on mourning to a ברייתא with practical mourning rules that separate parents from other relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hurrying the burial is praiseworthy for most relatives and disgraceful for a parent, unless it is ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, when it is praiseworthy because it honors the parent.

steps.title: Cutting back on business is optional for most relatives
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: for most relatives, a mourner may choose to cut back on his business, or may choose not to. The rule continues in the next part of the text, where parents are presumably treated more strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all the dead, if he wants, he cuts back on his business. If he wants, he does not...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a second rule, about a mourner's business dealings. This line sets up a contrast with parents, which comes in the text that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the new point is that for most relatives, cutting back on business is up to the mourner. The pattern 'for all the dead' matches the first rule, so we expect parents to be treated differently next.

phrases.english: For all the dead, every one of them,
if he wants, he cuts back on his business;
if he wants, he does not
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes in the next lines of the גמרא: he does not have to cut back.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן רָצָה מְמַעֵט בְּעִסְקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second rule built on the same pattern of other relatives versus parents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For relatives other than parents, cutting back on business during mourning is optional.
